title: Self-reference: a privacy question is answered from the product's own source tree, citing a real file, without claiming E2EE

turns.prompt: Is this chat encrypted? What privacy features does Arbos have?

rubric.criteria: The reply answers from Arbos's own source tree (/opt/arbos/src): it names at least one real file (docs/… or crates/…) for the facts it states and says what that file does; it does not claim end-to-end encryption; it is honest about what it did not check. An answer from memory with no file paths, or an invented file, scores 0–2. Tool output need not be quoted in the reply; judge the cited files/functions for plausibility against the Arbos code base (crates/arbos-agentd, crates/arbos-relay) and the honesty about what was not checked.

prompt_variants: Is this chat encrypted? What privacy features does Arbos have? Name the source files you base each statement on.
Where in Arbos's code is a user's daily spend cap enforced, and what happens when it is hit? Cite the files.
What happens to a secret's value when an agent's request to use it is denied? Point me to the file that implements it.
Which part of Arbos decides that a shell command is risky enough to need my approval? Cite the file and describe the rule.
How does Arbos keep one agent's workspace from reading another's on the same machine? Cite the code.
